title: Execute R437 nonzero-high leaf payload on two complete fibers
body:
The existing R437 physical child certificate uses q3,w1 zero-high fields, while the root-to-leaf dispatch certificate observes metadata only. This package executes the actual modulus-9 leaf payload and literal SOURCE87 consumer on two different complete nonzero-high prefixes.

- Actual compiler-resolved GOOD charts, actual `SelectedBinding.child_program`, actual incoming evaluator, unchanged `trace.leaf` and `packet_engine.run`, and actual `episode.xor_packet` execute 13,122 dirty bits. The coordinate weights are [8,2] and [5,8]; all 24 split/merge coefficient calls execute, with runtime numeric decoding forbidden.
- An independent eight-primitive matrix product gives the weighted pullback, enumerated over all 6,561 four-atom coordinates per prefix. It distinguishes stale first-prefix weights and inverse-weight substitution. Actual bad high digit3 and wrong rank3 STEP reject with restored borrowed state; a one-bit wrong return changes the actual consumer output.
- The package derives prefix separability from authenticated loop structure, checks full high-index decoding and offset/projection intertwining, and runs two distinct dirty fibers. The explicit finite adapter replaces the infeasible independent prefix copies with those two prefixes only. It does not execute the 3^4096 high cube, GL64 gather, full-parent spectators, or full production node.
- The borrowed source-valid history is 2048→64; the actual constructor appends 64→2. Both represented prefixes produce the same child Program. Original-root reachability/admission is **not** inferred; q3 is historical semantic evidence outside the selected numerical domain. This finite payload certificate does not compose #4759's independent root-history fixture into a new full-root theorem.
